explanations.answer: They welcome them joyfully
explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. The text says “…the brothers welcomed us joyfully.” Nobody's checking a watch or sizing anybody up. That's the kind of welcome where somebody grabs your bag before you can ask.

explanations.answer: They keep them waiting outside
explanations.explanation: No waiting room here, friend. Nobody leaves them standing on the porch. The text says the brothers welcomed them joyfully when they arrived. I know a thing or two about being left out of sight, and this is the opposite.

explanations.answer: They ask them to leave the city
explanations.explanation: Not at all, friend. Nobody is asking anybody to leave. The text says the brothers there welcomed them joyfully. It's about as far from a closed door as you can get.

explanations.answer: What God had done among the Gentiles through him
explanations.explanation: Right on target, friend. Gentiles are people who aren't Jews, and Paul recounted what God had done among them through his ministry. Notice whose work he's reporting on. He talks about what God had done. I'd have been so busy bragging about my cookies that I'd have burnt the batch.

explanations.answer: Every argument he had with people on the road
explanations.explanation: I get the pick, friend. A long trip makes for long stories. But the text says Paul recounted the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry. It doesn't say he went down a list of arguments.

explanations.answer: His plans for where he would travel next
explanations.explanation: Close to what a traveler might talk about, friend, but not what the text says. Paul went through the things God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry. He did it one by one. The text doesn't mention his next stops at all.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The text says that when they heard Paul's report, they glorified God. They heard what God had done, and their first move was to give Him the glory. That's a good habit to bake into your own day.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: Careful, friend. The text says, “When they heard this, they glorified God.” So James and the elders heard Paul's report and gave God the glory. This one is True.

explanations.answer: Moses
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Moses, Israel's leader, is the name in the text. The elders say the believers are under the impression that Paul teaches the Jews among the Gentiles to forsake Moses. Notice they say 'under the impression.' That's what they've heard, and it isn't the same as what Paul actually teaches.

explanations.answer: David
explanations.explanation: David, Israel's king, is a great name to reach for, friend. But the text says the believers think Paul teaches people to forsake Moses. David doesn't come up in that line. Pick the name that's in the verse and you're golden.

explanations.answer: Abraham
explanations.explanation: Abraham is the one God told to leave his home (Genesis 12:1), so I see why he came to mind, friend. But the elders name someone else here. The text says they think Paul teaches people to forsake Moses. The blank is Moses.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: Flip that one around, friend. The rumor says the opposite. The text says the believers think Paul tells the Jews among the Gentiles not to circumcise their children or observe their customs. So this one is False.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The rumor says Paul is telling them not to circumcise their children or observe their customs. Nobody is saying he tells them to keep circumcising. It's a rumor, and the elders say in verse 24 that there's no truth to it.

explanations.answer: Purify himself with them and pay their expenses
explanations.explanation: Exactly, friend. The elders tell Paul to take the four men, purify himself along with them and pay their expenses. That's two jobs in one sentence. The text says it's so the four can have their heads shaved.

explanations.answer: Send them out to preach among the Gentiles
explanations.explanation: That's a fine job, friend, but it isn't in the elders' advice. The text says to take the men, purify himself with them and pay their expenses. Nobody is sent anywhere in that verse.

explanations.answer: Bring them all before the high priest
explanations.explanation: The elders never mention the high priest, friend. They say to take the four men, purify himself along with them and pay their expenses. That's the whole assignment.

explanations.answer: The rumors about him are not true
explanations.explanation: You got it, friend. The elders say, “Then everyone will know that there is no truth to these rumors about you…” The plan is to show everyone that the rumors are false. They add that Paul also lives in obedience to the law.

explanations.answer: He is the leader of the church
explanations.explanation: That's not what the elders are after, friend. They say the plan will show that there is no truth to the rumors about Paul. It's all about the rumors, and nobody mentions who is in charge.

explanations.answer: He has finished his travels for good
explanations.explanation: Interesting guess, friend, but the elders don't say a word about travels here. They say that everyone will know there is no truth to the rumors about him. They also say he lives in obedience to the law.

explanations.answer: Food sacrificed to idols
explanations.explanation: Right, friend. The elders' list says the Gentile believers must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals and from sexual immorality. That's four things. They tell Paul they have already written this decision to them.

explanations.answer: Trading in the marketplace
explanations.explanation: Nothing about shopping or trading on that list, friend. The elders name four things: food sacrificed to idols, blood, the meat of strangled animals and sexual immorality. Marketplaces never come up.

explanations.answer: Travel on the Sabbath
explanations.explanation: The Sabbath isn't on this list, friend. The elders say the Gentile believers must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals and from sexual immorality. Travel isn't mentioned at all.

explanations.answer: Announce the date the offering would be made for each man
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. Paul enters the temple to give notice of the date when their purification would be complete. That is also when the offering would be made for each of them. It's a notice, like putting a pickup time on a cookie order.

explanations.answer: Teach the crowds in the courts about the Lord Jesus
explanations.explanation: Paul has taught plenty in other places, friend, but that's not what this verse says. He enters the temple to give notice of the date when their purification would be complete and the offering would be made for each man. Teaching the crowds isn't the errand here.

explanations.answer: Ask the high priest to bless the four men in private
explanations.explanation: The high priest never shows up in this verse, friend. Paul enters the temple to give notice of the date when the purification would be complete. That's also the date the offering would be made for each of the men.

explanations.answer: Stir up the whole crowd and seize him
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. These Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul at the temple, stirred up the whole crowd and seized him. They went from seeing him to grabbing him in no time at all. This is where a calm day turns into a hard one.

explanations.answer: Ask him to explain his teaching
explanations.explanation: I wish they had, friend. A little conversation goes a long way. But the text says they stirred up the whole crowd and seized him. Nobody asked a question first.

explanations.answer: Report him to James and the elders
explanations.explanation: James and the elders are back in the earlier scene, friend, and they aren't part of this one. The text says the Jews from Asia stirred up the whole crowd and seized Paul. They didn't go to anyone to report him.

explanations.answer: Bringing Greeks into the temple
explanations.explanation: That's the charge, friend. They cry out, “Furthermore, he has brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.” It's a serious thing to say about someone, and the next verse tells us where they got it.

explanations.answer: Taking money from the temple treasury
explanations.explanation: Not a word about money, friend. The text says they accuse Paul of bringing Greeks into the temple and defiling this holy place. That's the 'furthermore' they add.

explanations.answer: Speaking against the high priest
explanations.explanation: The high priest isn't named in their cry, friend. They say Paul teaches against their people, their law and this place. Then they add that he has brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The text says they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian, who traveled with Paul (Acts 20:4), with Paul in the city. Then they assumed Paul had brought him into the temple. They saw no such thing, so this one is False.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. They had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with Paul in the city, and the text says they assumed Paul had brought him into the temple. An assumption is only a guess that got loud. Nobody in the text says they saw Trophimus inside.

explanations.answer: temple
explanations.explanation: Right, friend. The people seize Paul and drag him out of the temple. After that, the text says the gates were shut at once. That's a hard scene, and I think this part of the story hurts.

explanations.answer: synagogue
explanations.explanation: A synagogue is a Jewish meeting place, friend, but this scene isn't at one. The text says the crowd drags Paul out of the temple. The blank is temple.

explanations.answer: marketplace
explanations.explanation: Marketplaces are busy, friend, but that's not where this takes place. The text says the people seize Paul and drag him out of the temple. After that the gates are shut.

explanations.answer: Runs down with soldiers and centurions
explanations.explanation: That's right, friend. The text says that immediately he took some soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd. Centurions are Roman officers. Nobody there is stalling.

explanations.answer: Waits for the crowd to calm down
explanations.explanation: Waiting would have been a long wait, friend. The text says that immediately he took some soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd. There was no pause for the commander.

explanations.answer: Sends one messenger to find out more
explanations.explanation: The commander goes himself, friend. He takes some soldiers and centurions and runs down to the crowd. The text says he does it immediately, with no messenger sent ahead.

explanations.answer: True
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The text says that when the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul. This is a heavy part of the story. The crowd had been beating him, and now they stop.

explanations.answer: False
explanations.explanation: I know that sounded believable, friend, but the text says the opposite. When the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul. This is a heavy moment, so I'm glad the text tells us they stopped.

explanations.answer: Who he is and what he has done
explanations.explanation: You got it, friend. After arresting Paul, the commander asks who he is and what he had done. Those are two fair questions. The answers just get buried under the noise that comes next.

explanations.answer: Where he has been staying in the city
explanations.explanation: That's a reasonable question for a commander, friend, but it isn't the one in the text. He asks who Paul is and what he has done. Where he's been staying doesn't come up.

explanations.answer: Who first brought him into the temple
explanations.explanation: Nobody in this verse gets asked that, friend. The text says the commander asks who Paul is and what he has done. The question is about Paul himself.

explanations.answer: barracks
explanations.explanation: That's right, friend. The commander can't get at the truth because of the uproar, so he orders Paul brought into the barracks. Barracks are where the soldiers stay. I know a little about being carried somewhere you didn't pick.

explanations.answer: palace
explanations.explanation: No palace in this scene, friend. The text says the commander orders that Paul be brought into the barracks. That's the soldiers' quarters, and it's what fills the blank.

explanations.answer: council
explanations.explanation: A council is a meeting, friend, and the text doesn't send Paul to one here. The commander can't get at the truth because of the uproar. So he orders Paul brought into the barracks.

explanations.answer: Because of the violence of the mob
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The text says Paul had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob. The soldiers had to lift him. I think this is the hardest picture in the whole passage, so I'm saying it plainly.

explanations.answer: Because the steps were blocked by guards
explanations.explanation: No guards are blocking anything, friend. The text says Paul had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob. The soldiers are the ones carrying him.

explanations.answer: Because the commander wanted him hidden
explanations.explanation: The text gives a different reason, friend. It says Paul had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob. It doesn't say the commander wanted to hide him, so I'm not going to add that.
